events.title: URI syntax standardized
events.summary: RFC 1630 defined Universal Resource Identifier syntax in June 1994 — a unifying scheme for naming and addressing objects on the web.
events.about: URIs label resources with a scheme (`http:`, `ftp:`, `mailto:`) and a path — the foundation of every link, API endpoint, and redirect. URLs and URNs are subsets of URI; browsers resolve `https://example.com/docs` because this document formalized the grammar. REST, OpenAPI, and CDN routing all assume URI-shaped identifiers.

narrative.whyChosen: RFC 1630 was Tim Berners-Lee's first IETF document unifying how the web names resources.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave HTTP, HTML, and DNS a shared addressing vocabulary that still underpins the web.
narrative.problemSolved: Early web software mixed incompatible naming schemes; hyperlinks needed one portable syntax.

sources.title: RFC 1630 — Universal Resource Identifiers in WWW (June 1994)
